"Cruel necessity." The night after King Charles I was beheaded, my Lord 'Southampton and a friend got leave to sit up by the body in the Banqueting House at Whitehall. As they were sitting there very melancholy at about two o'clock in the morning, they heard the tread of somebody coming slowly up the stairs. By-and-by the door opened, and a man entered very much muffled up in his cloak. He approached the body, considered it very attentively for some time, and then shook his head and sighed out the words "cruel necessity, " He then departed in the same slow and concealed manner as he had come in. Lord Southampton used to say that he could not distinguish anything of his face, but that by his voice and gait he took him to be Oliver Cromwell.
